futureYear12CandidatesOnly.scope: Concentration and introductory temperature/K reasoning subset. C4 pressure/catalysts, C5 expressions, C6 calculations, C9 temperature/K data and practical conduct separate.
futureYear12CandidatesOnly.proposedDescription:
What changes immediately when you add or remove a substance, and what changes later as the reactions respond? Follow concentration changes in a simple one-to-one model, then connect temperature to a different equilibrium mixture.

NSW Chemistry Stage 6 Syllabus (2017), Year 12 Module 5: Equilibrium and Acid Reactions. This lesson supports the concentration and temperature parts of Factors that Affect Equilibrium, with introductory temperature/equilibrium-constant reasoning. It is one part of the module sequence.
Official syllabus: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/chemistry-stage-6-2017

Entry knowledge: Dynamic equilibrium, equal opposing rates, concentration and balanced equations. Next: Gas pressure and volume, then catalysts in a separate lesson. Constructing equilibrium expressions, numerical calculations and temperature/K data are later videos. Required practical investigations remain separate.

The A/B model is schematic. Conditions and assumptions are stated on screen. Pause for the two prediction questions before the explanations.
